strengths: test_stop_gates.py is behavioral throughout. It arms real sentinels through the production path helpers (phase5_sentinel_dir, min_viz sentinel_dir_under) and runs both gates' real decide functions. Only the gate tuple is swapped in the fault-isolation test.
test_both_armed_block_once_with_both_reasons checks that stdout has exactly one non-blank line, which pins the single-decision contract, not just that both reasons appear.
test_stop_hook_active_allows_the_stop_for_both_gates counts two loop-break notices, which proves each gate saw the flag independently.
test_a_raising_gate_leaves_the_other_to_decide drives _guarded with a real exception and asserts both the surviving block and the stderr note.
The contract test moves Stop to stop_gates.py in EXPECTED and adds a COMPOSED entry, so the import-parity test now also guards stop_gates.py against drift.

When both gates block, their reasons are joined into the single JSON decision, so neither block reason is dropped and stdout still holds one decision object.

Splitting each gate into decide(payload, state_root) plus emit_block keeps both scripts runnable on their own. SubagentStop still registers check_min_viz_sentinel.py alone, and decide is testable without stdin.

important.name: Import-cost guard never runs main(), so a lazy jsonschema import passes
important.summary:
test_the_launch_imports_neither_pydantic_nor_jsonschema runs the hook with runpy.run_path(..., run_name='not_main'), so main() never executes and only module-level imports are measured. The stdin '{}' it sets up is never read. jsonschema is imported lazily inside harness_lib/config.py:_validate (line 328), which load_config calls. If state_root_for went back to load_config, which is the cost this change removes, the probe would still print [] and the test would pass. The docstring claims the guard covers 'the Stop launch', but it cannot fail for the most likely regression.

Also (roast): test_the_launch_imports_neither_pydantic_nor_jsonschema runs stop_gates.py through runpy with run_name='not_main', so main() never runs: only module-level imports are measured. Every jsonschema import in harness_lib is lazy (config._validate imports it inside the function), so the regression this PR removes (state_root_for calling load_config again) would pass this test untouched. Only the pydantic half can fail today; the jsonschema half is decoration. The probe even sets sys.stdin to '{}', which only matters if main runs. A Stop launch that silently gets its 90 ms back would sail through green.

Also (adv_code): test_the_launch_imports_neither_pydantic_nor_jsonschema runs stop_gates.py through runpy with run_name='not_main', so only module-level imports execute; main(), state_root_for and both decide() calls never run. harness_lib.config imports jsonschema lazily inside _validate, so the regression this PR removes (a schema-validated load_config on every Stop launch, the ~90 ms the check_phase5_sentinel docstring cites) can come back inside state_root_for or a gate and the test still reports []. The stdin it sets is also never read.

Attack: Reintroduce the old load: in plugins/harness/hooks/check_phase5_sentinel.py state_root_for (line 193 area) add `load_config(project)` before the return (import load_config from harness_lib.config at module top; that import itself stays stdlib-only). Run `python -m pytest tests/hooks/test_stop_gates.py -k imports_neither -q`: it passes, because run_name='not_main' skips main(). Reproduced in-process by docs/_scratch/pr_review/0327/pr327_20261120T054910Z/probes/lazy_import_probe.py, which wraps state_root_for with a load_config call: after import the heavy list is [] (what the test asserts), after stop_gates.main() it is ['jsonschema'].
fix: In the probe, keep run_name='not_main' and then call ns = runpy.run_path(...); ns['main'](). Before that, set sys.stdin to a JSON payload whose cwd is a make_project project that carries .claude/harness.json, so state_root_for's config-read path runs. Then assert sys.modules holds neither library.

Or run the hook as a real subprocess ([sys.executable, '-X', 'importtime', hook] or a wrapper that runs main and then prints the sys.modules check) with a Stop payload pointing at a make_project project.

Run the real entry point in the probe: build a project with make_project, set sys.stdin to a payload naming its cwd, call runpy.run_path(..., run_name='__main__') inside try/except SystemExit, then print the pydantic/jsonschema membership of sys.modules.

Alternatively run the probe as a subprocess of stop_gates.py itself with a sitecustomize-free wrapper that, after main returns, reports sys.modules (e.g. import the module, call module.main() with a patched stdin payload, then print).

Run the hook as __main__ in the probe (runpy.run_path(..., run_name='__main__') inside try/except SystemExit), feed stdin a payload whose cwd is a make_project directory (ideally with a valid harness.json and an armed sentinel so both gates walk their full path), then print the heavy-module list.
Alternatively call the loaded module's main() inside the probe after setting sys.stdin, before reading sys.modules.

minor.name: CLAUDE.md per-repository sentinel rule still names sentinel_dir_under as the Stop hook's anchor
minor.summary:
CLAUDE.md:43-45 says `sentinel_dir_under` anchors Phase 5 sentinels at the main checkout and that the Stop hook, `phase4_branch_safety.py`, the schema hook and `agent-watcher` use that rule ('change it in all four or none'). After this PR the Stop path no longer calls `sentinel_dir_under`: `check_phase5_sentinel.state_root_for` (plugins/harness/hooks/check_phase5_sentinel.py:255-263) builds `main_worktree(project) / state_dir` itself and `decide` appends `SENTINEL_SUBDIR` (:290). The result is the same today, but the anchoring rule now has a second copy the CLAUDE.md checklist does not name, so a later change made only in `sentinel_dir_under` (the function the rule points to) would silently miss the Stop and SubagentStop gates. The PR edited CLAUDE.md for the dispatcher but left this rule as written.

Also (roast): CLAUDE.md:43-45 says sentinel_dir_under anchors the sentinels and that the Stop hook uses that rule, 'change it in all four or none'. After this PR the Stop gates compute the location as main_worktree(project) / state_dir (state_root_for) plus SENTINEL_SUBDIR in each decide, a second spelling of the same anchor rule that the doc does not list. The behavior matches today; the next person changing the anchor in sentinel_dir_under will follow the doc and miss state_root_for.

Also (roast): CLAUDE.md:41-42 states that scripts, hooks and skill commands call activate(load_config(project_root(...))) once. The Stop gates (check_phase5_sentinel.py, check_min_viz_sentinel.py, stop_gates.py) deliberately stopped doing so for launch cost and read state_dir raw instead. Nothing on the gate path reads active() today, so it works, but the rule in the project doc is now contradicted by the same PR with no stated exception; a later gate that calls active() would load and validate the config lazily and quietly undo the speedup.
fix: Update CLAUDE.md:43-45 to name the Stop hook's copy, e.g. '`sentinel_dir_under` (and, for the Stop and SubagentStop gates, `check_phase5_sentinel.state_root_for` plus `SENTINEL_SUBDIR`) anchors them at the main checkout'.

Or keep a single anchor in code: have `check_phase5_sentinel.decide` take the project and call `sentinel_dir_under(project, raw_state_dir)` (stdlib-only, already in `artifact_names`), leaving CLAUDE.md as written.

Add a stdlib helper (e.g. state_root_under(project, state_dir) returning main_worktree(project) / state_dir) to validation/artifact_names.py, have both sentinel_dir_under functions and state_root_for call it, and name it in CLAUDE.md:43.
Or update CLAUDE.md:43-45 to name check_phase5_sentinel.state_root_for as the Stop hook's copy of the anchor rule that must change with sentinel_dir_under.

Add an exception to the 'Drivers activate, library code reads' rule in CLAUDE.md: the Stop gates read state_dir raw through check_phase5_sentinel.state_root_for, never activate, and their decide path must not call active().

minor.name: state_root_for re-implements the sentinel_dir_under anchor
minor.summary: state_root_for (check_phase5_sentinel.py:263) builds main_worktree(project) / state_dir inline. Both gates previously reached their folder through sentinel_dir_under (artifact_names.py:46-53 and min_viz_sentinel.py:24-27), which the writers (phase4_branch_safety.py:270, min_viz_sentinel.arm) still use. The project rule names sentinel_dir_under as the per-repository anchor shared by the Stop hook, phase4_branch_safety.py, the schema hook and agent-watcher. The Stop side now has a second copy of that anchor, so a change to sentinel_dir_under would move the writers' folder while the Stop gates keep scanning the old one. The result is the same today, but the shared-rule guarantee no longer holds by construction.
fix: Return sentinel_dir_under(project, state_dir).parent from state_root_for (both gate subdirs are single leaf names), so the Stop hook keeps going through the shared anchor.
Add a state_root_under(project, state_dir) helper in validation/artifact_names.py that returns main_worktree(project) / state_dir. Have both sentinel_dir_under functions and state_root_for call it.
